# Commands

Every command takes `--book` to say which book of record to work on. It
defaults to `shearstud.sqlite3` in the working directory and is never read
from the environment, because a rating office runs one book per district.

## Groups

| Group       | What it covers                                                          |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `book`      | Look after the book of record itself.                                   |
| `campaign`  | Measurement campaigns.                                                  |
| `fatigue`   | Fatigue evaluation.                                                     |
| `gauge`     | Gauges on the structures.                                               |
| `program`   | The inspection programme: intervals, priority and the worklist.         |
| `report`    | Print what the book holds, for one structure or for the district.       |
| `structure` | Look at and change the inventory.                                       |
| `thickness` | Ultrasonic readings, and what they leave of the section.                |
| `vehicle`   | The rating vehicles: what is in the fleet and what each one looks like. |

## Detail

### `shearstud init`

Create the book of record, or bring an existing one up to date.

### `shearstud status`

Report the schema version and what the book holds.

### `shearstud check`

Run the structural checks SQLite can do on the book itself.

### `shearstud book prune`

Remove superseded conclusions older than a cutoff.

    Each structure keeps its newest rating and posting and each detail keeps
    its newest evaluation, whatever the cutoff says. A structure last rated in
    1998 loses nothing.

| Option     | Default | What it does                                       |
| ---------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `--before` |         | Cutoff date, YYYY-MM-DD. Nothing newer is touched. |
| `--yes`    |         | Actually remove the rows. Without it, nothing is.  |
| `--vacuum` |         | Rebuild the file afterwards to reclaim the space.  |

### `shearstud book orphans`

Spectra whose gauge is no longer in the book.

    Always empty on a book this package has written, because the foreign key
    cascade takes them. It is worth asking after a restore, which is the one
    route by which they appear.

### `shearstud book vacuum`

Rebuild the file, giving back the space a prune freed.

### `shearstud book counts`

How many rows are in each table.

### `shearstud gauge list`

Every gauge in the book.

| Option     | Default | What it does                   |
| ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------ |
| `--detail` |         | Only the gauges on one detail. |

### `shearstud gauge add`

Record a gauge installation.

Takes `gauge_id`, `detail_id`.

| Option          | Default        | What it does                                         |
| --------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `--installed`   |                | Date the gauge was bonded, YYYY-MM-DD.               |
| `--orientation` | `longitudinal` | Which way the grid runs relative to the girder axis. |
| `--factor`      | `2.1`          | Gauge factor.                                        |
| `--limit`       | `1500.0`       | Channel limit, ue.                                   |
| `--removed`     |                | Date the gauge came off, YYYY-MM-DD.                 |

### `shearstud campaign list`

Campaigns on one structure, oldest first.

Takes `number`.

### `shearstud campaign add`

Record a measurement campaign.

Takes `campaign_id`, `number`.

| Option       | Default | What it does               |
| ------------ | ------- | -------------------------- |
| `--from`     |         | First day, YYYY-MM-DD.     |
| `--to`       |         | Last day, YYYY-MM-DD.      |
| `--seasonal` | `1.0`   | Seasonal factor.           |
| `--note`     | ``      | What the campaign was for. |

### `shearstud spectrum`

Read a two column range and count file into the book.

Takes `campaign_id`, `gauge_id`, `counts`.

| Option        | Default | What it does      |
| ------------- | ------- | ----------------- |
| `--bin-width` | `5.0`   | Bin width, ue.    |
| `--dropout`   |         | Dropout fraction. |
| `--railed`    |         | Railed fraction.  |

### `shearstud fatigue evaluate`

Evaluate every detail on a structure against one campaign.

Takes `number`, `campaign_id`.

| Option                 | Default | What it does                                                |
| ---------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--growth`             |         | Override the recorded traffic growth.                       |
| `--allow-poor-records` |         | Evaluate untrustworthy records too.                         |
| `--save`               |         | Write the evaluations into the book.                        |
| `--condition`          | `7`     | Lowest component condition rating from the last inspection. |

### `shearstud record`

Read a raw strain file, condition it, and count the cycles in it.

Takes `campaign_id`, `gauge_id`, `strain`.

| Option           | Default | What it does                                                   |
| ---------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--rate-hz`      |         | Sample rate the logger was set to.                             |
| `--limit-ue`     |         | Channel limit. Defaults to the one recorded against the gauge. |
| `--bin-width-ue` | `5.0`   | Spectrum bin width.                                            |
| `--trigger-frac` | `0.35`  | Event trigger, as a fraction of the conditioned peak.          |
| `--events`       |         | Print a line per truck event.                                  |
| `--save`         |         | Write the spectrum into the book.                              |

| `--detour-mi` |         | Miles of detour if the structure closes.               |
| `--posted`    |         | Whether a weight limit is up.                          |
